proof_attempt_summary: The run proved an exact full-kernel identification criterion for coordinated interventions in canonical latent LiNGAMs, extending the comparator to arbitrary finite latent-source counts with zero or proportional redundancy and no moment assumptions. Mathematical review passed, the two imported theorems were verified against primary sources, and the construction/maximality audit found no further in-scope theorem strengthening. The result nevertheless remained subfield-level because it is population/exact-real only, lacks finite-sample stability or recovery guarantees, and offers only a narrow concrete application; a field-level continuation would require a genuinely new research direction rather than another D0 repair.
tldr: The full kernel for a specified coordinated intervention is identified exactly when every eligible latent noise replacement has zero post-intervention outcome residual. Equal observed descendants govern path-faithful rivals; minimal observed descendancy governs unrestricted acyclic rivals. The minimal-descendant criterion now covers arbitrary finite latent counts and zero or proportional redundant candidate source columns, with no candidate moment assumption. A single swap witnesses failure, while a columnwise argument handles every feasible simultaneous assignment. The exact residual yields a generic blocking rule and a polynomial exact-real population test. A two-node fork separates competitor classes; a three-node family shows joint identification despite singleton nonidentification.
gap: The published singleton equal-descendant test in Tramontano et al. 2024 is incompatible with a canonical cancelling rival allowed by its literal unknown-graph Eq. (7). Existing faithful support-group arguments and later proxy, instrument, and general-confounding results do not establish an exact coordinated full-kernel criterion for all acyclic same-law canonical rivals.
